event.title: Statewide Caregiver Support Group: Virtual
event.description:
Caregiving can be both deeply meaningful and incredibly challenging. It is common to feel rewarded and overwhelmed at the same time. You may sometimes feel like no one truly understands what you are going through, but you are not alone. We understand, and support is available.

Caregiver Support Groups bring together people with shared experiences to offer encouragement, understanding, and practical insight. These groups provide emotional and social support, a chance to learn what has worked for others, and information about helpful local resources.

Free to attend, this is an online support meeting available statewide in Alaska on the second and fourth Thursday of each month. You may join by phone or Zoom and attend one meeting or continue coming as often as you find helpful.

event.title: Statewide Grief Support Group
event.description:
We most often think of grief as a response to the death of someone close. It is that, but it is more. For caregivers, it issomething that is continuous, daily, often lasting for years before the passing of the one for whom they’re providing care. In the emotionally jumbled, stressful experience of being a caregiver, who listens and understands? Alzheimer’s Resource Alaska does, and we are
offering a place and time for caregivers to be heard, to share thoughts and feelings, and find solace. Join us.

We offer compassionate grief support groups on the first and third Thursdays of each month, led with care by Gay Wellman through Zoom. We welcome anyone navigating the loss of a loved one, as well as caregivers and others who continue to experience anticipatory grief due to Alzheimer’s disease or another form of dementia.

Because the groups meet online, people from communities across the state can come together to share stories, receive understanding, and find comfort in the company of others who truly get what they are going through. Whether your grief is fresh or something you have carried for a while, you will find a place here where your feelings are honored and you do not have to face them alone.

You are welcome just as you are.

With questions or to sign up, reach out to Gay Wellman at gwellman@alzalaska.org.

event.title: Art Links – Fairbanks (in-person)
event.description:
Come and share the joy of Art Links with us in Fairbanks! Art Links is a social support program that promotes engagement for individuals diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias or seniors at risk of isolation and depression. By using a variety of creative art ideas, we promote self-expression as well as socialization and meaningful connections. Participants enjoy:

  • A variety of artistic mediums
  • Music and movement
  • Memory-rich conversations
  • Facilitated by ARA staff and local artists.

Free to attend! No registration required. Share with friends and family. With questions, contact Jennifer Willeford at JWilleford@alzalaska.org or 907-621-6071.

Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Color Bash
event.description:
Following the runaway success of Glow-N-Fire — named the Pollstar Family Show of the Year — Color Bash takes the action to a whole new level, transforming the arena into a full-throttle collision of color. Vibrant paint-splattered trucks, bursts of color, and electrifying lighting turn every smash, and crash, into a vivid spectacle the whole family can see, feel, and remember.

When the mischievous Skelesaurus drains all the color from Monster Truck Island, it’s up to the crew of Rhinomite™, Mega Wrex™, Tiger Shark™, Bone Shaker™, and Bigfoot® to win it back — one massive stunt at a time, Every wheelie, jump, donut and freestyle run brings the color roaring back, building to a full-arena burst of light, sound, and pure Monster Truck energy. It’s the show you love, reimagined like you’ve never seen it.

“Color Bash is the most vibrant Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Live experience we’ve ever created,” said Ken Hudgens, CEO, Family Entertainment Live. “We took everything fans love about the show — the massive trucks, the jaw-dropping stunts, the can’t-look-away energy — and supercharged it with color. It’s a brand-new way to experience the action live, and we can’t wait to bring it to families in [CITY] in 2027.”

In 1976, with the release of the Bill Murata-produced Poki Records album, No Kristo, alongside appearances at Kapahulu’s Uptown Yokos, Jerome Koko, Louis “Moon” Kauakahi, Skippy Kamakawiwoʻole, Israel Kamakawiwoʻole, and Sam Gray – collectively, The Mākaha Sons of Niʻihau, introduced Hawai’i to their highly influential, contemporized music style, firmly rooted in the language and traditional performances of their native Hawai’i.

Unlike several contemporaries, who’s Top 40 radio-friendly songs were written in English and performed with contemporary instruments, The Mākaha Sons of Niʻihau celebrated Hawai’i and its language in both arrangements and vocal styling. Their dedication to hana kuʻuna, traditional works, has ignited and inspired generations of performers to embrace the journey.

Though the group has evolved through the ensuing five decades – most notably with the loss of Skippy and the departure of Israel – the core members have shared the stage with both minted members and guest artists in live and recorded performances. With Israel’s 1993 departure for his solo career, the group’s name changed to The Mākaha Sons, but the music stayed true to the group’s core principles.

Among their accolades are some thirty studio and live albums, several Na Hoku Hanohano Awards and Hawaii Music Awards, The Makaha Bash sell-out concerts at the Waikiki Shell, appearances on national television shows, and concert tours and

appearances at prestigious venues and events throughout the nation, including the inaugural activities for former U.S. President Barack Obama.

The Mākaha Sons will celebrate their 50th anniversary on Saturday, July 18, 2026, at Blaisdell Arena, together with some very special guests.

Reserved tickets, priced from $35 to $150*, go on sale Friday, May 8th at Blaisdell Box Office and Ticketmaster. The link to ticket sales: https://www.ticketmaster.com/makaha-sons-50th-anniversary-honolulu-hawaii-07-18-2026/event/0A006491C489B03E

JO KOY BIOGRAPHY 2026
As one of today’s premiere stand-up comedians, Jo Koy has come a long way from his modest beginnings performing in a Las Vegas coffee house. Jo’s uniquely relatable comedy pulls inspiration from his colorful family that has reached all kinds of people and has translated into sold-out arenas around the world.

The comedian continues to be one of the top 10 grossing stand-up comedians each year according to Pollstar and Billboard. Today, he continues selling out and breaking sales records at some of the most prestigious venues around the world including Mall of Asia Arena (Manila, PH), The Forum (Los Angeles), Coca-Cola Arena (Dubai), ICC Theatre (Sydney, AU), O2 Arena (London), Madison Square Garden (New York City), and American Airlines Arena (Dallas) to name a few. In 2022, Koy kicked off his Funny Is Funny World Tour by selling-out the Climate Pledge Arena (over 14,000 tickets) in his hometown of Seattle and ended the tour with a sold-out show at Tacoma Dome (over 19,000 tickets). In 2017, Koy broke a record for the most tickets sold by a single artist at 23,000 tickets and 11 sold-out shows at The Neal S. Blaisdell Concert Hall in Honolulu. In response, the mayor’s office in Honolulu proclaimed November 24th as “Jo Koy Day.”

Koy starred in the 2022 Universal Picture comedy Easter Sunday, the film takes place around a struggling single father that returns to his hometown of Daly City, CA to survive a chaotic Easter with his family. The film is a love letter to his Filipino roots and is loosely based on Jo Koy’s life experiences and stand-up comedy. Easter Sunday was produced by Steven Spielberg’s production company Amblin Partners and is the first motion picture film to feature an all-Filipino cast and be produced by a major studio. In honor of the film, Daly City gave Jo the Keys To The City and declared July 22nd “Jo Koy Day.”

In 2023, Koy appeared in Disney’s Haunted Mansion and voiced characters in Netflix’s animated films, Monkey King and Leo. In 2024, he was most recently heard voicing the character Monkey King in the Paramount+ film, The Tiger’s Apprentice. He’s also appeared in Netflix’s Mr. Iglesias and Comedy Central’s Awkwafina Is Nora from Queens.

In 2023, it was announced that he inked a two-special deal with Netflix with the first special releasing in 2024. Jo returned to Netflix in typical style, sharing his unfiltered opinions on social media, aging and moving into a new phase of his life; his zaddy phase. Filmed at the historic King’s Theatre in Brooklyn, NY, Jo Koy: Live From Brooklyn premiered globally on June 4th, 2024 only on Netflix and reached the Top 10 within the first week. His other Netflix stand-up specials include Live From The Los Angeles Forum, Comin’ In Hot and Live From Seattle. Overall, Koy has had seven highly rated and successful specials on Comedy Central and Netflix. In June 2020, the comedian released his first variety special, Jo Koy: In His Elements on Netflix in which Koy brings the laughs and beats to Manila, spotlighting local culture in a one-of-a-kind show featuring Filipino-American comedians, DJs and B-boys.

On March 21st, 2026, Koy alongside Gabriel “Fluffy” Iglesias will become the first to headline and sell-out SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles for their One Night Only! show.

Koy continues to push for representation in Hollywood and shine a light on Filipino talent. Last year Koy joined Nurse Unseen, a documentary from Emmy-winning director Michele Josue, as an executive producer. The film explores the little-known history and humanity of the unsung Filipino nurses who risked their lives on the frontlines of the COVID-19 pandemic while facing a resurgence of anti-Asian hate in the streets.

In honor of Koy’s impact on Hollywood and comedy, his legacy was permanently cemented during a hand and footprint ceremony at the TCL Chinese Theatre on February 11, 2026, joining an elite group of distinguished talent.

In 2023, Jo came on as a producer for the David Byrne-Fatboy Slim musical, Here Lies Love. Here Lies Love told the story of Imelda Marcos’ rise to power and subsequent fall at the hands of the Philippine People Power Revolution. The show received four Tony Award nominations during its run and was the first to feature an all-Filipino cast on Broadway.

In 2022, Koy was once again acknowledged for his advocacy for more representation in entertainment and was given the proclamation in Los Angeles that October 7th would be declared “Jo Koy Day.”

JO KOY BIOGRAPHY 2026
As one of today’s premiere stand-up comedians, Jo Koy has come a long way from his modest beginnings performing in a Las Vegas coffee house. Jo’s uniquely relatable comedy pulls inspiration from his colorful family that has reached all kinds of people and has translated into sold-out arenas around the world.

The comedian continues to be one of the top 10 grossing stand-up comedians each year according to Pollstar and Billboard. Today, he continues selling out and breaking sales records at some of the most prestigious venues around the world including Mall of Asia Arena (Manila, PH), The Forum (Los Angeles), Coca-Cola Arena (Dubai), ICC Theatre (Sydney, AU), O2 Arena (London), Madison Square Garden (New York City), and American Airlines Arena (Dallas) to name a few. In 2022, Koy kicked off his Funny Is Funny World Tour by selling-out the Climate Pledge Arena (over 14,000 tickets) in his hometown of Seattle and ended the tour with a sold-out show at Tacoma Dome (over 19,000 tickets). In 2017, Koy broke a record for the most tickets sold by a single artist at 23,000 tickets and 11 sold-out shows at The Neal S. Blaisdell Concert Hall in Honolulu. In response, the mayor’s office in Honolulu proclaimed November 24th as “Jo Koy Day.”

Koy starred in the 2022 Universal Picture comedy Easter Sunday, the film takes place around a struggling single father that returns to his hometown of Daly City, CA to survive a chaotic Easter with his family. The film is a love letter to his Filipino roots and is loosely based on Jo Koy’s life experiences and stand-up comedy. Easter Sunday was produced by Steven Spielberg’s production company Amblin Partners and is the first motion picture film to feature an all-Filipino cast and be produced by a major studio. In honor of the film, Daly City gave Jo the Keys To The City and declared July 22nd “Jo Koy Day.”

In 2023, Koy appeared in Disney’s Haunted Mansion and voiced characters in Netflix’s animated films, Monkey King and Leo. In 2024, he was most recently heard voicing the character Monkey King in the Paramount+ film, The Tiger’s Apprentice. He’s also appeared in Netflix’s Mr. Iglesias and Comedy Central’s Awkwafina Is Nora from Queens.

In 2023, it was announced that he inked a two-special deal with Netflix with the first special releasing in 2024. Jo returned to Netflix in typical style, sharing his unfiltered opinions on social media, aging and moving into a new phase of his life; his zaddy phase. Filmed at the historic King’s Theatre in Brooklyn, NY, Jo Koy: Live From Brooklyn premiered globally on June 4th, 2024 only on Netflix and reached the Top 10 within the first week. His other Netflix stand-up specials include Live From The Los Angeles Forum, Comin’ In Hot and Live From Seattle. Overall, Koy has had seven highly rated and successful specials on Comedy Central and Netflix. In June 2020, the comedian released his first variety special, Jo Koy: In His Elements on Netflix in which Koy brings the laughs and beats to Manila, spotlighting local culture in a one-of-a-kind show featuring Filipino-American comedians, DJs and B-boys.

On March 21st, 2026, Koy alongside Gabriel “Fluffy” Iglesias will become the first to headline and sell-out SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles for their One Night Only! show.

Koy continues to push for representation in Hollywood and shine a light on Filipino talent. Last year Koy joined Nurse Unseen, a documentary from Emmy-winning director Michele Josue, as an executive producer. The film explores the little-known history and humanity of the unsung Filipino nurses who risked their lives on the frontlines of the COVID-19 pandemic while facing a resurgence of anti-Asian hate in the streets.

In honor of Koy’s impact on Hollywood and comedy, his legacy was permanently cemented during a hand and footprint ceremony at the TCL Chinese Theatre on February 11, 2026, joining an elite group of distinguished talent.

In 2023, Jo came on as a producer for the David Byrne-Fatboy Slim musical, Here Lies Love. Here Lies Love told the story of Imelda Marcos’ rise to power and subsequent fall at the hands of the Philippine People Power Revolution. The show received four Tony Award nominations during its run and was the first to feature an all-Filipino cast on Broadway.

In 2022, Koy was once again acknowledged for his advocacy for more representation in entertainment and was given the proclamation in Los Angeles that October 7th would be declared “Jo Koy Day.”

In 2021, Koy released his first autobiography, Mixed Plate: Chronicles of an All-American Combo with Harper Collins Publishers to raved reviews. A mother. A daughter. 3 possible dads.

On the eve of her wedding, a daughter’s quest to discover the father she’s never known brings three men from her mother’s past back to the island they last visited decades ago.

For over 25 years, people all around the world have fallen in love with the characters, the story, and the music that make MAMMA MIA! the ultimate feel-good show.

Surel’s Place honors the legacy of artist Surel Mitchell (a founding member of BOSCO) by offering her home and studio to artists of promise, and of renown, for month-long residencies and professionally supported art events. This event aims to enhance public understanding of the artistic process, foster connections, and build community.

event.title: WORKSHOP: FOUND FAMILIES
event.description:
@

WORKSHOP
FOUND FAMILIES
Saturday, October 17th | 1:00pm – 4:00pm
$45

REGISTER

This collage workshop with Artist-in-Residence Eli Craven focuses on re-interpreting family image archives through alterations and combinations with additional found and made materials. We explore family photography and portraiture, the meanings they carry, and how we can transform them through these added materials. You may use additional materials such as thread, fabric, papers, documents, wood, mirrors, metals, etc. As we create collages and tell stories, we will also discuss the meaning behind the combinations of these materials and how images change over time.

You are encouraged to bring some of your own materials to work with: copies and test strips, in addition to originals of photographs intended to use in the workshop. A variety of found photographic images and various sources will also be available.

Partial scholarships available by request to info@surelsplace.org.

BIOGRAPHY

Although currently based in Indiana, Eli Craven was raised in Idaho. “Returning to Idaho for this project feels appropriate given the origins of my relationship to photography and a return to the subject matter of my childhood,” Eli says. In his childhood home, magazines and movies were censored, select films and TV shows were forbidden, sexuality and death were seldom discussed. The power images hold was discovered through scrutinizing forbidden magazine collections, daytime soap operas, and movies. The impetus of his practice resides in this desire to see, only to discover nothing shocking. Instead, seemingly mundane imagery is isolated and fragmented, presenting a narrative exploring the image’s role in processes of socialization.

Eli left Idaho with a BFA in photography from Boise State back in 2011. He went on to pursue an MFA in photography at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. Currently an Associate Professor of Photography at Purdue University, his work has been widely exhibited and published. Most recently his work has been exhibited at Kant Gallery in Copenhagen, Denmark; KlompChing Gallery in Brooklyn, New York; and at the Blue Sky, Oregon Center for the Photographic Arts in Portland, Oregon.

event.description:
@

EXHIBIT & ART TALK
A PLEA FOR TENDERNESS
Thursday, October 29th | 7:00pm – 8:30pm
free

In this project Eli Craven aims to position the viewer as a collaborator or partner in the physical experience of the work. Viewers are invited to alter photographic compositions through a series of kinetic elements and reflective materials, including sliding wood panels, hinged doors, and movable peepholes. The viewer must engage and activate the framing components to reveal the photographic image, potentially provoking the desire to see what is hidden within. Participation is integral to this project, with entire scenes rendered incomplete without the viewer’s touch and imagination filling the gaps and visualizing what lies beneath the surface of the photograph, or behind the veil.

Although the works exist within the canon of photography, they are sculptural objects that utilize the photograph as part of their construction. Eli’s work started with an obsession for photography and its materials and that fixation remains at the core of his practice.

Upcoming Pop-in Program themes:

[/et_pb_text][et_pb_accordion _builder_version=”4.27.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”][et_pb_accordion_item title=”October: Potion Power” open=”on” _builder_version=”4.27.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}”]One Saturday session: October 31 | 1-5pm

Potion Power: The Magic of Chemistry

This Halloween, enter a world of bubbling brews and mysterious mixtures as we uncover the real science behind classic potion-making! This month’s Pop-In Program uses a STEAM-focused approach to explore fizzy reactions, color-changing concoctions, and ingredients that behave in surprising ways. Participants will investigate the chemistry hidden inside spooky “witch’s brews” and magical transformations.
[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”November: Pendulums! The Swing of Science” _builder_version=”4.27.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” open=”off”]Two Saturday sessions: November 7 & 28 | 1-5pm

The Swing of Science: Exploring the Power of the Pendulum

Discover how a simple swinging weight helped scientists understand motion, time, and the forces that shape our world! This month’s Pop-In Program uses a STEAM-focused approach to explore how pendulums move, what affects their swing, and why Galileo’s observations changed science forever. Participants will test different pendulum designs and experiment with patterns and timing.
[/et_pb_accordion_item][et_pb_accordion_item title=”December: It’s the Most Wonderful SLIME of the Year” _builder_version=”4.27.0″ _module_preset=”default” global_colors_info=”{}” open=”off”]One Saturday session: December 5 | 1-5pm

It’s the Most Wonderful Slime of the Year

Get ready to stretch, squish, and explore science! Kids will dive into the chemistry of polymers and cross-linking while creating their own colorful, sparkly slime—a non-Newtonian fluid that behaves like both a solid and a liquid. It’s messy, hands-on fun with a STEM twist!
[/et_pb_accordion_item][/et_pb_accordion][et_pb_text admin_label=”Text” _builder_version=”4.27.0″ background_size=”initial” background_position=”top_left” background_repeat=”repeat” custom_margin=”48px|||||” hover_enabled=”0″ global_colors_info=”{}” sticky_enabled=”0″]

Watch the 1975 cult classic like never before…with a Medieval Studies expert! The Museum of Idaho and Idaho State University invite you to a rare film screening of Monty Python and the Holy Grail, followed by a discussion with Dr. Thomas Klein, ISU English Professor with a PhD in Medieval Studies.

About Dr. Klein: As philologist, Dr. Klein is interested in early medieval writing and how knowledge is represented in physical form. Recently, he has written a series of articles on Anglo-Saxon riddles and inscribed objects, including the Franks Casket, the Staffordshire Hoard, and the Vindolanda tablets.

Doors open at 6:30 pm  |  Program starts at 7 pm 

Discounts

  • Enrolled ISU students get free admission for themselves. Select the ISU student ticket option at checkout. Please be sure to include your student ID on the checkout form!
  • Active MOI members: use code MEM3 to receive $3 off each ticket.
  • ISU faculty and staff: use code ISU3 to receive $3 off each ticket.

This film is rated PG.

Location: ISU Idaho Falls Campus, Tingey Auditorium (1776 Science Center Dr)

event.description:
A limited-time monthly series where kids search for clues and solve mysteries in the exhibits. Two sessions are available on the same Saturday each month: juniors ages 6 to 9, and detectives ages 10 to 13.

Galileo: Mystery of the Experimental Mind

A scientific mystery is waiting to be uncovered. Step into the world of Galileo, the pioneering thinker whose experiments transformed astronomy, motion, and the study of machines. Kids will investigate clues from his bold ideas, explore evidence from his observations and inventions, and use their imagination to piece together the story of a mind that helped ignite the birth of modern science!

Sessions:

  • Juniors (ages 6-9): 1:30-2:30 pm  |  Register
  • Detectives (ages 10-13): 3-4 pm  |  Register

Registration opens 30 days before each monthly session.

General admission is not included

event.title: Museum Mysteries
event.description:
A limited-time monthly series where kids search for clues and solve mysteries in the exhibits. Two sessions are available on the same Saturday each month: juniors ages 6 to 9, and detectives ages 10 to 13.

Petroglyph Wall: Mystery of the Ancestral Echoes

A cultural mystery is waiting to be uncovered. Join us as we explore Bailey Dann’s powerful artwork inspired by Shoshone-Bannock ancestral petroglyphs and stories passed down through generations. Kids will look closely at the shapes, figures, and patterns carved into the metal panels, consider how these markings help protect history, and imagine the echoes of stories carried through time. With the artist present to share her perspective, participants will gain a deeper understanding of how art continues the work of ancient story keepers!

Sessions:

  • Juniors (ages 6-9): 1:30-2:30 pm  |  Register
  • Detectives (ages 10-13): 3-4 pm  |  Register

Registration opens 30 days before each monthly session.

General admission is not included

Bio
James Jaxxa’s multi-faceted practice explores themes of memory, desire, vulnerability, community and pleasure through the creation of bedazzling personal reliquaries and cathartic shrines. His work is influenced from growing up nomadically in a military family, Catholic iconography and queer culture.

He received his MFA from the School of Visual Arts, his BS from Michigan State University and completed post-baccalaureate work at School of the Art Institute of Chicago and Rhode Island School of Design. He has attended residencies at Barac (Mannheim, Germany), Salzburg International Summer Academy (Salzburg, Austria), R.A.R.O. (Barcelona, Spain), Berlin Art Institute (Berlin, Germany) and others.

Jaxxa’s work has been shown in exhibitions across the United States and internationally including those at Terrain Biennial, New York Public Library, The LGBT Center in New York, University of Nevada, Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Seattle Art Museum, Bellevue Art Museum and numerous other institutions and galleries. His public artwork, Potential Connections was installed for the inauguration of Seattle’s Link Light Rail system. Jaxxa has been included in publications by The New York Times, Visual AIDS, New York Public Library and The Seattle Times. He was awarded an Artists Space Independent Project Grant.

Jaxxa is a founding member of I Found U, an international group of artists working across different materials and mediums, committed to discussion and collaboration on environmental, sociological and economic concerns. He lives and works in New York City.

event.title: Broadway Comes To Bradley II
event.description:
Broadway Comes To Bradley II
October, 3, 2026 at 7:30pm in the Meyer Jacobs Theatre

For one night only… Broadway performer and Bradley University Theatre Arts Performance alum Morgan Siobhan Green, along with award-winning composer and lyricist Joe Iconis, are coming to Bradley!

After last year’s triumphant Broadway Comes to Bradley, in which Morgan performed alongside Tony and Pulitzer Prize winner Michael R. Jackson (A Strange Loop), we are thrilled to bring Morgan back again, along with another of her dear friends from the world of Broadway: composer and lyricist Joe Iconis.

Morgan was one of Bradley Theatre’s all-time best actors, excelled on BU’s Speech Team, and performed in Broadway’s Be More Chill and in the US National Tour of the smash-hit Broadway musical Hadestown.

Joe’s highly acclaimed musical Be More Chill was nominated for numerous Tony, Drama Desk, and Outer Critics Circle awards. This prolific artist has also written the music and lyrics for the musicals Broadway Bounty Hunter and Love in Hate Nation, and developed the musicals The Untitled Hunter S. Thompson Musical and Punk Rock Girl, among many other projects.

Morgan and Joe, along with Bradley’s Theatre Arts and Music students, will perform an evening of original music that is sure to delight and inspire.

Tickets can be purchased in-person at the Hartmann Center box office, or online.

Please join us for Broadway Comes to Bradley II – an exciting evening of music and fun!

event.title: BSides Peoria 2026
event.description:
Join the Illinois Cyber Foundation and the Center for Cybersecurity at Bradley University for BSides Peoria 2026, a one-day, community-driven cybersecurity conference bringing together professionals, students, educators, researchers and enthusiasts for a day of learning, hands-on exploration and collaboration.

Returning to Bradley on Saturday, Oct. 24, BSides Peoria features 15 technical talks, a dedicated keynote from Alethe Denis, hands-on villages, competitions and networking opportunities spanning a wide range of cybersecurity topics.

Attendees can explore the Physical Security Village, Human Hacking Village and Radio Frequency Village, with activities covering lockpicking and physical access controls, social engineering and human behavior, wireless technologies and RF security. Competitions include the BSides Peoria Capture the Flag, Vishing Challenge, Zero Trust, and Phish Bowl, offering opportunities for both experienced participants and newcomers to test their skills.

BSides events are built by the cybersecurity community, for the cybersecurity community, emphasizing accessible learning, conversation and participation. The Center for Cybersecurity has hosted BSides Peoria at Bradley University since the conference was established by the Illinois Cyber Foundation in 2023.

Whether you work in cybersecurity, are preparing to enter the field, or are simply curious about how technology can be attacked and defended, BSides Peoria offers opportunities to learn something new, meet others in the community and get hands-on with cybersecurity.

Registration is required. Visit BSidesPeoria.com for tickets, conference updates and additional information.

event.title: Henry IV, Part 1 by William Shakespeare
event.description:
Henry IV, Part 1 by William Shakespeare
November 5 – 15, 2026 in the O’Sullivan Studio Theatre
Directed by Debbie Alley

Bradley returns to the O’Sullivan Studio Theatre for a mainstage production for the first time since 2017 with Henry IV, Part One, a Shakespearean masterpiece about King Henry IV’s struggle with rebellious nobles (particularly Henry “Hotspur” Percy), while his son, Prince Hal, navigates a wild life with the roguish Falstaff, before proving his worth.

This history play, written around 1597, covers the period from late 1402 to mid-1403 and explores themes of honor, rebellion, and father-son relationships, contrasting the king’s disappointment in Hal with his envy of Hotspur’s gallantry. The production will be guest-directed by Debbie Alley, a nationally respected theatre artist and educator.

event.title: Eyewitness to History: Inside the Presidency with Pete Souza – Voices & Visionary Series
event.description:
Go behind the scenes of the presidency with Pete Souza as he shares iconic photos and stories from inside the White House.

Step inside the most powerful office in the world with renowned White House photographer Pete Souza.

As the only photographer to serve as Chief Official White House Photographer for both Presidents Barack Obama and Ronald Reagan, Souza offers a rare behind-the-scenes look at the presidency through the lens of his camera. Over decades in the White House, he captured defining moments of leadership, crisis, and humanity, many of which have become iconic images in modern American history.

In Eyewitness to History: Inside the Presidency, Souza shares unforgettable photographs and the stories behind them, offering a candid and deeply personal perspective on what it is really like to document history as it happens.

This special event is part of OLLI at Bradley University’s Voices and Visionaries series, bringing influential voices and extraordinary experiences to our community. Parking will be free on campus for all attendees.

Event Registration: Free

Bio
James Jaxxa’s multi-faceted practice explores themes of memory, desire, vulnerability, community and pleasure through the creation of bedazzling personal reliquaries and cathartic shrines. His work is influenced from growing up nomadically in a military family, Catholic iconography and queer culture.

He received his MFA from the School of Visual Arts, his BS from Michigan State University and completed post-baccalaureate work at School of the Art Institute of Chicago and Rhode Island School of Design. He has attended residencies at Barac (Mannheim, Germany), Salzburg International Summer Academy (Salzburg, Austria), R.A.R.O. (Barcelona, Spain), Berlin Art Institute (Berlin, Germany) and others.

Jaxxa’s work has been shown in exhibitions across the United States and internationally including those at Terrain Biennial, New York Public Library, The LGBT Center in New York, University of Nevada, Newhouse Center for Contemporary Art, Seattle Art Museum, Bellevue Art Museum and numerous other institutions and galleries. His public artwork, Potential Connections was installed for the inauguration of Seattle’s Link Light Rail system. Jaxxa has been included in publications by The New York Times, Visual AIDS, New York Public Library and The Seattle Times. He was awarded an Artists Space Independent Project Grant.

Jaxxa is a founding member of I Found U, an international group of artists working across different materials and mediums, committed to discussion and collaboration on environmental, sociological and economic concerns. He lives and works in New York City.

event.title: Spectroscopy as Cultural Heritage
event.description:
Dr. Roger Turner will present a talk highlighting the fascinating history of cultural practices and social groups on the field of spectroscopy, the scientific study of how matter interacts with electromagnetic radiation. His talk introduces some of the hidden figures who helped make spectroscopy a powerful technique that scientists use to understand the compositions of cultural heritage objects—including paintings, textiles, archeological artifacts, photographs, contemporary art, and much, much more. Women like Clara Smith Craver created the books of chemical “fingerprints” that identify different materials, while groups of scientists learned to how to do spectroscopy through summer courses at Fisk University, a historically Black university. Surprising objects from the Science History Institute museum reveal that spectroscopists can be playful and silly, while doing work that has transformed our understanding of art and archeology. Dr. Turner is the curator of instruments and artifacts at the Science History Institute in Philadelphia.

This is the keynote lecture for the IRUG Conference taking place at Winterthur October 7–9. IRUG is a group dedicated to the use of infrared and Raman spectroscopies applied to cultural heritage. Included with admission. Members free.

event.description:
Join conservators and conservation graduate students from the Winterthur/University of Delaware Program in Art Conservation for a hands-on workshop about how to care for your cherished objects in hazardous flood conditions. Participants will have the opportunity to learn a variety of processes from freezing and drying books to safely removing heavy, wet textiles from flood waters.

event.title: Objects Up Close Virtual Series
event.description:
Portrait of Catherine de Visme Browne

When Henry Francis du Pont purchased this portrait and installed it prominently in Montmorenci Stair Hall, it was identified simply as an “American Empire Portrait.” Yet it is not a mere likeness. This portrait of Catherine de Visme Browne by Ezra Ames depicts a young woman of great intellect, beauty, and ability, and also presents an embodiment of taste and moral character within the cultural aspirations of the nation. It offers an authoritative statement—first for the Browne family and later for du Pont—about cultural refinement and aspiration, as expressed through material depictions. The talk is presented by Kayleigh Danowski, Lois F. McNeil Fellow, Winterthur Program in American Material Culture. Registration required. Free.

event.title: Research at Winterthur Speaker Series
event.description:
A Nation Unraveled

During the American Civil War, clothing became central to the ways people waged war and experienced its cost. Through the clothes they made, wore, mended, lost, and stole, Americans expressed their allegiances, showed their love, confronted their social and economic challenges, subverted expectations, and, ultimately, preserved their history. As the collections they left behind make clear, Civil War Americans believed clothing was not merely a reflection of one’s class, gender, race, military rank, political ideology, or taste. Instead, Northerners and Southerners alike understood that clothing—from the weave of a fabric to the style and make of a coat—had the power to affect people’s way of living through the war’s tumult. In this lecture, Sarah Jones Weicksel discusses her new book, A Nation Unraveled: Clothing, Culture, and Violence in the American Civil War Era (University of North Carolina Press), a material history of war.  

The Research at Winterthur series, presented by the Library, Research Fellowship Program, and Continuing Education, showcases new projects and publications that tap into our rich collections and resources, unveiling innovative perspectives for exploring the fascinating stories that objects can tell about people and our shared past. Registration required. Included with admission. Members free. Lecture followed by book signing.

Register now.

America’s First Woman Botanist

event.title: Stitched In Place: Needlework Conference
event.description:
March 19–21, 2027

Stitched in Place is a two-and-a-half-day conference that invites you to consider how place is not only a backdrop but a central thread in the story of American needlework. Join us to examine how Americans have used needlecraft and sewn and embroidered objects, whether stitched in schoolrooms, parlors, or workshops, to understand and communicate how they see the world and their places in it.

The conference will include research presentations, panel discussions, workshops for all interests and skill levels, special tours, and other exciting opportunities to engage with Winterthur’s extraordinary needlework collection.  

Participants will see behind-the-scenes in the Needlework Study room, visit our Textile Conservation Lab, learn how Winterthur protects and preserves its collections, and learn about scalable ways to bring those practices into your own home and collections. 

Registrants can sign up for a multiday workshop led by leading needle artists, learn more about our fantastic collections, and discover ways you can begin your own journeys of making and collecting.

Designed for a variety of audiences, Winterthur welcomes seasoned embroiderers, collectors, and those curious and eager to learn more. This conference draws its theme from an exhibit of the same name.

About the Exhibit

Stitched in Place, on view through April 4, 2027, explores how American needlework has and continues to serve as a medium for expressing identity, belonging, and awareness of place. Featuring approximately twenty objects from Winterthur’s collection, including  samplers, needlework pictures, hatchments, tools, garments, accessories, and furnishing textiles from the seventeenth through twentieth centuries, this installation invites reflection on how makers used needle and thread to communicate who they were, where they came from, and how they wished to be seen.

Stitched in Place is presented as part of Winterthur’s ongoing Conversations with Collections series in the Galleries.

event.title: Winterthur Institute
event.description:
April 4–16, 2027

Intended for professionals in the care of cultural heritage, graduate students, and scholars of American decorative arts, this two-week immersive experience includes lectures, hands-on workshops, research opportunities, and access to the specialists, gardens, and historic architecture of Winterthur.

Participants will be part of a select cohort that engages in daily study of Winterthur’s world-renowned collection, with contextualization in the history of American decorative arts, object materiality, and techniques of museum stewardship. Upon completion of Winterthur Institute, participants will have gained:

  • historical knowledge of the decorative arts, as well as techniques of cultural analysis, which define the relationship of an object to its time.
  • competency in best practices for handling objects, as demonstrated in a preventive conservation practicum with Winterthur’s collections.
  • an understanding of “sense of place” while studying collections in the former du Pont historic home and estate.
  • 70 hours of professional development in key skills and knowledge for cultural heritage study.
  • support of the Winterthur learning community and a stronger professional network.
  • a certificate of completion.
For more information and to apply, visit winterthurinstitute.org.
Winterthur Institute is supported by Learning Times, LLC; The Decorative Arts Trust; and Winterthur Institute alumni.

event.title: Men’s Concert & Dance Fall 2026
event.description: There is an old German saying: wo man singt, da lass dich nieder — where there is singing, settle in and stay. As the days grow shorter, the men of the Indianapolis Liederkranz invite you to do exactly that at our Fall Concert & Dance on Saturday, October 24, 2026. Doors open at 5:30 pm, the concert begins at 7:00 pm, and dancing follows. (Music provided by Charlie’s Pocket.) Come for the singing and stay for the evening — a tradition the Liederkranz has kept since 1872. Wir freuen uns auf Sie!

event.title: Damenchor Bunter Abend 2026
event.description:
Bunter Abend means “colorful evening,” and that is exactly what the Damenchor has in store. Join us Saturday, November 7, 2026, for an evening of music and good company in the best Liederkranz tradition. Doors open at 5:00 pm and the show begins at 7:00 pm. Bring your friends, bring your neighbors, and come ready for a lively night — bunt wie das Leben, colorful as life itself. Wir freuen uns auf Sie!

Music after the concert will be provided by the Liederkranz German band!

event.title: Children’s Christmas Party 2026
event.description: Bring the little ones to the Liederkranz for our Children’s Christmas Party on Sunday, December 6, 2026, from 2:00 to 4:00 pm. December 6 is Nikolaustag — St. Nicholas Day — the day German children wake to find their boots filled with sweets and small gifts, and we will be keeping the tradition in style. Expect music, treats, and an afternoon of good cheer for the whole family. Wir freuen uns auf Euch!

event.title: Art Center Café, Dinner with Friends: Deidre and Marvin DeJear – SOLD OUT
event.description:
We are excited to continue the Art Center Café’s signature culinary experience: Dinner with Friends. Be our guest as we gather around the table with friends for a lighthearted evening of laughter, conversation, and live music in the cozy setting of the café. Each dinner features a unique menu inspired by our special guest hosts and prepared by the Art Center Café’s Executive Chef Stephanie Williams.

For the second installment of our fall dinner series, we’re welcoming Deidre and Marvin DeJear. Deidre is the President and CEO of Oakridge Neighborhood Services and Marvin is a local entrepreneur, advocate, and mentor. Their dinner draws inspiration from the couple’s travels across coastal regions – from the Gulf to Asia and the Hawaiian Islands – unified through the creative vision of Chef Williams. Join us for an evening that brings together food, community, and the stories that connect us. The event will also include live music by Napoleon Douglas.

Upcoming Dates:
October 15: Tar and Erika Macias

$125/person; all-inclusive.

Reservations are required; payment will be taken on the night of the event. Tickets include a four-course meal and beverages. First seating begins at 5 pm and seating ends at 6:15 pm. Please share any dietary restrictions when making your reservation. Limited capacity. Tables seat six; smaller parties will be seated together for a festive evening of community and togetherness.

This dinner is sold out. For questions or to join the waitlist call 515.271.0313 or email cafe@desmoinesartcenter.org.

event.title: “Artists on Fire” Exhibition Tour
event.description:
Join us for a free guided tour of the exhibition “Artists on Fire,” on view in the John Brady Print Gallery September 5, 2026 – January 10, 2027. This selection of prints, drawings, and photographs from the permanent collection explores the element of fire, both literal and conceptual. Images of flames, smoke, and steam sit alongside depictions of Greek gods and visions of hell.

Free; no registration required.

event.title: Art for Brunch!
event.description:
We invite you to join us at Art for Brunch! Come hang out with us at this monthly meetup for adults of all ages and enjoy thoughtful conversation as we unpack a different work of art each month. A docent will guide the dialogue with questions and prompts, but each discussion will be as unique and varied as those who attend. We’ll go where the conversation leads us. No art background needed. Just bring your curiosity and a willingness to look a little longer.

*While we would typically encourage participants to visit the Art Center Café before or after the program, the Café will be closed Sunday, October 4 for a private event. We apologize for any inconvenience.

Art for Brunch! is held on the first Sunday of each month. Free; registration required.

REGISTER

event.title: 2026 Fingerman Lecture: Alison Saar
event.description:
We invite you to join the Des Moines Art Center in welcoming artist Alison Saar as the featured speaker of our annual Fingerman Lecture series. Saar’s work examines the place of the female body in the realms of politics and spirituality. She explores Black female identity, and the powerful, multifaceted roles women play — from everyday life to timeless, legendary figures.

Saar has exhibited artworks at many galleries and museums throughout the United States. Her art is represented in the collections of the Whitney Museum of American Art, the Baltimore Art Museum, the Museum of Modern Art, and the Metropolitan Museum of Art. Her 1997 piece, “Sweeping Beauty” was added to the Des Moines Art Center’s permanent collection in 2003.

REGISTER

The Fingerman Lecture series is made possible through generous gifts by Lois and the late Dr. Louis Fingerman. Alison Saar is the 36th installment in the series.

Free; registration required.
Photo: Alison Saar

event.title: Creative Aging: Gallery Series (Ages 55+)
event.description:
Creative Aging is a program designed for adults age 55+ to gather at the Art Center and learn about art while making community connections and fostering cognitive health. During this gallery series, an Art Center docent will lead the group in collaborative discussion, focusing on one work of art. Following the gallery talk, guests are invited to an informal social time with coffee and tea.

Creative Aging is a free, monthly program at the Art Center. There are multiple registration times available; each program will last approximately 90 minutes. Registration is required; gallery seating is available.

REGISTER

event.title: Social Saturday: Monster Mash
event.description:
Join the Des Moines Art Center’s October Social Saturday event: Monster Mash! Enjoy crafts in the Art School studios, Fright Night with Final Act Ensemble, a scavenger hunt, a guided tour, spooky storytime, treats in the Art Center Café, and so much more.

We invite you to dress for the season and come in costume!
Please dress appropriately for a family friendly event. Consider safety and security when choosing your outfit. Avoid tails, wings, costume props or inflatable elements that could accidentally damage artwork as you walk through the galleries. Costume masks and replica weapons are not allowed. Our security team has the right to refuse any costume entering the museum.

Schedule of Events:

11:15 – 11:30 am | Spooky Storytime (all ages)
Levitt Auditorium
1 pm | Guided Tour (all ages)
Meet in the Macomber Lobby
1:30 pm | Fright Night with Final Act Ensemble
The Des Moines Community Playhouse’s Final Act Ensemble brings ghosts, witches, murder, and mystery to life in a Halloween performance inspired by the golden age of radio. *Please note: This program may not be suitable for young children.
Levitt Auditorium

Drop-in Activities (11 am – 2 pm):

Museum Galleries

  • Find the Social Saturday interactive Art Cart in the galleries.
  • Complete a scavenger hunt in the galleries and return your findings to the front desk for a small prize.

Macomber Lobby

  • Enjoy the Art Center’s Paint-n-Play station.

Art School Studios

  • Explore creativity and your inner artist! Free drawing available in the studio space, as well as a unique Social Saturday: Monster Mash activity with jack-o’-lanterns and monster hand-puppets.

Art Center Café

  • Stop by for a sit-down lunch, a delicious pastry, and a full coffee and tea menu. Art Center members receive a  10% discount in the café. Be sure to grab a special  la mie monster cookie for Social Saturday: Monster Mash!

Museum Shop

  • Browse the Museum Shop to find gifts and souvenirs. Art Center members receive a  10% discount in the Museum Shop. Don’t miss the clearance section or the $10 and under table!

See our special exhibitions!

  • “Elle Pérez: La Despedida” (A. H. Blank Gallery)
  • “Artists on Fire” (John Brady Print Gallery)
  • “Valentin Noujaïm: La Défense” (Pamela Bass-Bookey and Harry Bookey Gallery)

Social Saturdays occur at the Des Moines Art Center on the second Saturday of the month. This event is free to attend, and no registration is required. Social Saturdays will be documented with photography.

For programs in Levitt Auditorium:
We strive to provide live captioning for all events offered in Levitt Auditorium. Due to interpreter shortages throughout Iowa, American Sign Language interpretation is only available upon request. ASL and other accommodation requests can be made by emailing jfeatherstone@desmoinesartcenter.org.

Generous support provided by Art Bridges Foundation’s Access for All program.

Support is provided by the National Endowment for the Arts and the Iowa Arts Council, which exists within the Iowa Economic Development Authority.

event.title: Fright Night with Final Act Ensemble
event.description:
Welcome to Fright Night at the Art Center! The Des Moines Community Playhouse’s Final Act Ensemble brings ghosts, witches, murder, and mystery to life in a Halloween performance inspired by the golden age of radio.

The evening features three chilling tales: “The Woman Who Wouldn’t Die,” in which a man begins to suspect his wife may be a witch burned more than 200 years ago; a spooky story of stranded teenagers, a possible dead body, and a mysterious stranger; and “The Moonlit Road,” Ambrose Bierce’s classic tale about a man who discovers the terrifying truth behind his mother’s murder.

For nearly 20 years, the Final Act Ensemble—a company of older adult actors—has performed polished old-time radio shows throughout the Des Moines area. This production features live acting, music, and sound effects.

Free; no registration required. Run time: approximately 50 minutes.

Please note: This program may not be suitable for younger children. The stories include death, murder, supernatural themes, eerie music, and spooky sound effects. Although portions of the performance are humorous, some children may find the program frightening.

event.title: Art Spectrums
event.description:
The purpose of Art Spectrums is to enable children and teens with autism, along with their families, to enjoy the Des Moines Art Center and make memories with art. In this program, kids, ages 5 – 18, on the autism spectrum and their family members explore and make art together. Participants will visit and discuss a work of art in the museum for inspiration. Next, attendees make their own artwork in the studio, inspired by what they discovered in the Art Center galleries.

Art Spectrums is a free, monthly program, and registration is required.

REGISTER

event.title: Art in the Dark – Flashlight Tour
event.description:
Experience the Des Moines Art Center at the Art in the Dark – Flashlight Tour. This after-hours adventure will leave you howling for more!

event.title: “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way” Curator and Artist Discussion
event.description:
Join the Des Moines Art Center for an invigorating discussion about the traveling exhibition organized by the Buffalo AKG Art Museum, “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way: Contemporary Latinx Painting,” which is on view at the Art Center from October 24, 2026, through January 24, 2027. Inspired by a 2008 poem of the same name by former US Poet Laureate Juan Felipe Herrera, “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way” celebrates the vision and creativity of Latinx painters. It showcases 58 artists who actively enrich the landscape of contemporary painting, introducing new approaches to form, materials, and subject matter.

Dr. Andrea Alvarez, curator of the exhibition, will provide insight into the premise of the show and introduce us to three of the featured artists: Danielle De Jesus, Justin Favela, and Patrick Martinez.

REGISTER

Danielle De Jesus is a Nuyorican painter and photographer born and raised in Bushwick, Brooklyn, whose woks tell the story of growing up in New York City amid gentrification and displacement. De Jesus’s background is in photography, and she utilizes her images of people native to Bushwick as a reference to tell the story of the community’s displaced residents.

Justin Favela is based in Las Vegas and is known for large-scale installations and sculpture that manifest his interactions with American pop culture and the queer Latinx experience. Favela explores traditional Mexican and Latin American craft — specifically cartoneria (a traditional Mexican folk art form that involves three-dimensional objects using papier-mâché and cardboard) — and his interest in art history, community, celebration, and home inform a practice intent on dismantling institutional hierarchies. Visitors may remember Favela from his 2021 exhibition at the Art Center, “Central American.”

Patrick Martinez maintains a diverse practice that includes mixed-media landscape paintings, neon signs pieces, cake paintings, and his Pee Chee series of appropriative works. His landscape paintings composed of Los Angeles surfaces — distressed stucco, spray paint, window security bars, vinyl signage, ceramic tile, and neon sign elements — evoke place and socioeconomic positions, unearth sites of personal and cultural loss. He lives and works in Los Angeles.

Free; registration required.

event.title: Day of the Dead / Día de Los Muertos
event.description:
Day of the Dead 2026: ¡Sí Se Puede!

Join us for the 26th annual Día de los Muertos at the Des Moines Art Center—our largest community celebration of the year. Rooted in Mexican tradition, Día de los Muertos is a time to gather in remembrance, honoring loved ones who have died through joy, ritual, storytelling, food, art, and shared celebration. The Art Center is pleased to help create space for this meaningful community tradition each year.

This year’s theme centers on civil rights, inspired by the phrase ¡Sí Se Puede! (“Yes, we can”), created by Dolores Huerta for the United Farm Workers movement. Together, we honor the people and collective efforts that have strengthened Latino communities in Iowa and across the United States, while reflecting on the power of gathering, shared purpose, and community care.

Visitors will enjoy live music and dance performances, food and art vendors, hands-on art activities, a festive Catrina photo opportunity, a community ofrenda, and a short documentary film featuring this year’s honoree, Felicia Timotea Leon Mullin. Free hot cocoa and samples of pan de muerto will be available while supplies last, and a complimentary shuttle will run from Merrill Middle School for easy parking.

Inspired in part by the Art Center’s current exhibition “Let Us Gather in a Flourishing Way: Contemporary Latinx Painting,” this year’s event reflects gathering, belonging, and the ways communities care for one another. In partnership with Progress Iowa and other community organizations, we’ll also recognize local leadership and the collective work of building stronger communities.

At its heart, Día de los Muertos at the Art Center is about community. It’s a space where art, culture, memory, and shared tradition bring people together. The Des Moines Art Center is proud to be a welcoming and inspiring cultural space for all.

Take advantage of easy parking and a free shuttle from Merrill Middle School, running continuously from 11 am to 3 pm.

event.title: Honoring the Spirit: A Day of the Dead Ofrenda Conversation
event.description:
Join the Des Moines Art Center for an exploration of what it means to honor the spirit — of loved ones, of cultural traditions, and of movements that have advanced justice and strengthened our communities.

At the center of the conversation is this year’s Day of the Dead ofrenda, created by poet and artist Michaela Mullin, in honor of her mother, Felicia Leon Mullin, and alongside local organizations which are continuing to advance the quality of life for all Iowans. Through the ofrenda and this year’s theme, Sí Se Puede!, panelists will consider how we remember those who have contributed to civil and human rights work, how their values live on through the people and communities they influenced, and why this work remains urgent today.

Opening with a brief Know Your Rights presentation led by Karina Sanchez of the Des Moines Civil and Human Rights Commission, this program will feature a conversation with Mullin; Vince Valdez, historian, filmmaker, and longstanding Day of the Dead committee member; and Erica Johnson, the founding Executive Director of Iowa Migrant Movement for Justice. Art Center Senior Manager of Museum Learning and Engagement, Mia Buch, will moderate. Join us for an inspiring conversation about remembrance, immigrant rights, community action, and carrying the work of previous generations forward.

event.title: A Taste of ReelAbilities
event.description:
The ReelAbilities Film Festival is the largest festival in the US dedicated to promoting awareness and appreciation of the lives, stories, and artistic expressions of people with disabilities. Founded in New York City in 2007, the festival presents international and award-winning films by and about people with disabilities in multiple locations throughout each hosting city. The 2026 Des Moines festival, “A Taste of ReelAbilities,” is a screening of recent short films during the Art Center’s November Social Saturday: Friendsgiving. All films will provide open captions and have audio description capabilities.

Generous support provided by Art Bridges Foundation’s Access for All program.

Free; no registration required.

Screening Information:
Film: A Morning with Aroha, 2021
Director: Nicholas Rini
Run Time: 11 minutes
Description: Aroha, an imaginative young girl with Down syndrome, sets out to share her creativity with her neighbors.

Film: Key of Genius, 2026
Director: Daniel Persitz
Run Time: 12 minutes
Description: Based on the extraordinary true story of Derek Paravicini, a blind, autistic musical prodigy, KEY OF GENIUS follows the bond between Derek and his dedicated piano teacher. Through patience, intuition, and unwavering belief, Derek’s hidden potential is unlocked, revealing the transformative power of music and mentorship. This film celebrates talent, perseverance, and the ways people with disabilities can flourish when given opportunity and understanding. Audiences are invited into a journey of inspiration, emotional depth, and triumph, witnessing a remarkable story of human connection, creativity, and the extraordinary capabilities that lie within those societies often underestimated.

*The following films are intended for adult audiences.

Film: Boys, 2026
Director: Olive Bilic
Run Time: 7 minutes
Description: Overwhelmed by the chaos of class, neurodiverse teenager Jacob seeks refuge in an empty locker room, only to face an unexpected confrontation. Created in collaboration with Bus Stop Films participants in Melbourne, BOYS highlights the emotional and social challenges faced by neurodiverse youth. Through authentic performances and an intimate lens, the film portrays the tension, vulnerability, and resilience of its characters, exploring the fine line between isolation and connection. BOYS is both a poignant and engaging narrative, offering insight into neurodiverse experiences while emphasizing the universal desire for understanding, acceptance, and human connection.

Film: Little Monsters, 2026
Director: Pablo Leridon
Run Time: 14 minutes
Description: A visually impaired teen navigates first love while sharing a transport van with a wheelchair-bound classmate. LITTLE MONSTERS blends humor and heart, showcasing adolescence, rivalry, and inclusive friendship.

Film: Bad Survivor, 2026
Director: Alex Dvorak and Katie North
Run Time: 11 minutes
Description: After being “broken up with” by her oncologists, a sarcastic young cancer patient begins her first day in remission, navigating the challenges of returning home. With humor and biting honesty, she confronts her family dynamics, cultural expectations, and the lingering trauma of treatment. BAD SURVIVOR balances comedy and pathos, portraying survival not as a singular triumph but as a process filled with awkward moments, personal reflection, and familial tension. Audiences are drawn into an intimate portrait of post-cancer life, where resilience, wit, and emotional vulnerability coexist, redefining what it means to move forward after illness.

Film: Don’t Take this the Wrong Way, 2026
Director: Rachel Handler and Crystal Arnette
Run Time: 7 minutes
Description: Darcy, beaten down by microaggressions and a recent breakup, begins to unravel emotionally. DON’T TAKE THIS THE WRONG WAY presents a raw exploration of personal vulnerability, societal pressures, and coping with isolation. The short captures moments of introspection, tension, and resilience, offering audiences an intimate glimpse into the lived experience of an amputee navigating social and emotional challenges. Through concise storytelling and authentic performances, the film conveys the complexity of identity, self-esteem, and the subtle ways everyday interactions can shape one’s emotional landscape.

Film: Misfit, 2026
Director: Tristan Zerbib
Run Time: 13 minutes
Description: In a world where disability is the norm, wheelchair-ball dominates the sports scene. A player is thrown off balance when forced to train with a ‘valid’ athlete, challenging her expectations and assumptions. MISFIT turns conventional sports narratives upside down, celebrating empowerment, inclusion, and the unpredictability of competition. Through fast-paced action and engaging character work, the film explores societal perceptions of ability and the courage required to embrace difference. MISFIT is a bold, energetic story that champions physical resilience, adaptability, and teamwork while entertaining audiences with humor, tension, and the triumph of spirit.

Film: Rearranged, 2025
Director: Liz Whitmere
Run Time: 12 minutes
Description: Set within the intimate confines of a hospice, REARRANGED explores how irritation, vulnerability, and humor can unexpectedly give way to human connection. Led by blind actor Bruce Horak, the film challenges assumptions about care, agency, and intimacy, revealing how small disruptions can reshape relationships.

Film: Them That’s Not, 2025
Director: Mekhai Lee
Run Time: 19 minutes
Description: Andrea “Drea” Stoney, a Deaf poet, attends her grandmother’s repass and navigates a family that doesn’t understand ASL. Complicating matters, her father is temporarily released from prison for the day, forcing Drea to reconcile with him amid grief. THEM THAT’S NOT explores identity, communication, and familial tension, highlighting the challenges Deaf individuals face within hearing-centered spaces. Through introspection, subtle humor, and emotional honesty, the film portrays the resilience required to carve personal space and connection, offering audiences insight into Deaf culture, intergenerational dynamics, and the quiet power of language, love, and understanding.

Due to interpreter shortages throughout Iowa, American Sign Language interpretation is only available upon request. ASL and other accommodation requests can be made by emailing jfeatherstone@desmoinesartcenter.org at least two weeks in advance. We will try to accommodate requests with less than a two week notice but cannot guarantee availability.

event.title: Unveil: Presented by the Museum Shop
event.description:
You are invited to our biggest Museum Shop event of the year, Unveil! Join us for an exclusive preview of newly acquired merchandise at this Winter Wonders shopping event. Items from this collection will not appear again until later in the year so plan some holiday shopping for everyone on your list (and yourself!). Enjoy complimentary small bites and festive, seasonal beverages with holiday cheer.

Unveil is open to anyone in the community; Art Center members receive double-discounts on all purchases.* Become a member today to receive your discounts!

This event is free to attend, and registration is not required. *Exclusions apply to consignment and clearance items.

event.title: Art Workshop: Greeting Cards, Thinking of You
event.description:
Get creative in this one-day workshop with the opportunity to make a unique design for your loved ones through greeting cards with ink, watercolor, and collage. Have fun, be inspired, and show off your creations with fellow class participants.

REGISTER

Des Moines Art Center members receive a 20% discount on all classes, camps, and workshops! Become a member today. 

Scholarships for classes and materials are offered on our application page.

event.title: Creative Aging: Studio Series (Ages 55+)
event.description:
Creative Aging is a program designed for adults age 55+ to gather at the Art Center and learn about art while making community connections and fostering cognitive health. These sessions will offer a social atmosphere and a variety of exploratory projects to try out materials and techniques with the support of an experienced teaching artist.

In this session, students will get creative with abstract drawing.

Materials, tools, and guidance will be provided. Cost of the class is $30 ($24 for Art Center members).

REGISTER

event.title: Little Slam on the Prairie Puppet Performance
event.description:
The Uplifting Puppet Co. is proud to present the return of Little Slam on the Prairie. This year’s event is hosted at the Des Moines Art Center as part of December Social Saturday: Make Believe.

This eclectic afternoon of short-form puppetry celebrates innovation, storytelling, and creative connection. Part of the national Puppet Slam Network, the show invites established puppeteers, artists new to puppetry, and theatre-makers to explore and  perform. From shadow theatre and object performance to giant puppets, comedy, multimedia, and avant-garde creations, Little Slam on the Prairie invites artists and audiences alike into an afternoon of imagination and surprise.

Free; registration required.

REGISTER

Little Slam on the Prairie is funded in part by a grant from the Puppet Slam Network, with additional support from the Des Moines Art Center and the Uplifting Puppet Co..

Social Saturday at the Des Moines Art Center receives generous support provided by Art Bridges Foundation’s Access for All program. Support is also provided by the National Endowment for the Arts and the Iowa Arts Council, which exists within the Iowa Economic Development Authority.

event.title: Family Art Workshop: Cardboard Gingerbread House
event.description:
Grab the whole family and dive into a season of hands-on creativity! This one-day art workshop is a perfect chance to make something new together. Artists of all ages are welcome. In this holiday season session, skip the frosting and build your dream gingerbread house out of cardboard, using a mix of playful materials to decorate it your way.

event.title: Cars & Coffee
event.description: Start your month the fun way at Cars & Coffee, held the first Saturday of every month at 9:00 a.m. Join us for coffee and donuts—and most importantly, a parking lot full of cool cars. Bring your ride to show off, or come stroll and check out what others drive. Enjoy free museum admission until 11:00 a.m., and stick around afterward for our Tread Talk.

event.title: Art + Car Culture from a Rat Fink Artist- October Tread Talk
event.description:
Get ready to dive into the colorful and creative world of Rat Fink and Kustom Kulture with artist Dan-O!
Inspired by legendary artist Ed “Big Daddy” Roth and the Kustom Kulture scene, Dan-O has been creating art since elementary school. During this special Tread Talk, he’ll share his journey as an artist, what inspired him to become a Rat Fink artist, and the history behind the Kustom Kulture movement.
Dan-O’s artwork has been featured in magazines, books and coloring books, and he currently has 36 pieces in the Rat Fink Museum. He’ll also bring along some of his artwork and share stories about his experiences as an artist in the car show world.
Whether you’re a longtime Rat Fink fan, an admirer of Kustom Kulture, or simply interested in the connection between cars and art, this is a Tread Talk you won’t want to miss!
Come early for our monthly Cars & Coffee and stay for this great presentation! Free admission to the museum until 11 a.m.

event.title: Tailgate & Tractor Show
event.description:
Join us for an afternoon celebrating the people and machines that help feed America!
The Tailgate & Tractor Show at Midwest Dream Car Collection will be an afternoon filled with tractors, great food, live music, family activities, and FREE museum admission all day!
Whether you’re a lifelong farmer, a tractor enthusiast, or just looking for a fun family outing, you’ll enjoy:
 Antique & Modern Tractor Display
 Cookout
 Live Music
 Fun Fall Activities
 Cornhole Tournament
 FREE Admission to the Midwest Dream Car Collection
 Bring Your Tractor!
We’re inviting owners of both antique and modern tractors to display their machines. Whether it’s a beautifully restored classic or the newest model in the field, we’d love to have you join the show.
Come celebrate agriculture, community, and the equipment that has shaped generations. Bring the whole family—we’ll see you at the museum!

event.title: British Invasion: Members-Only Reveal
event.description:
The British are coming… and our members get the first look!

Join us for an exclusive Members-Only Reveal of British Invasion, our newest exhibit celebrating the charm, style and spirit of classic British automobiles.

Be among the first to explore the new exhibit featuring a collection of iconic British cars, including a special showcase of MG sports cars. Enjoy an up-close look at the vehicles, discover their stories, and get a sneak peek before British Invasion opens to the public. Drinks and appetizers will be served. Enjoy live music as you stroll the exhibit.

This special evening is our way of saying thank you to the members who help make Midwest Dream Car Collection possible! Membership has its perks — including being first through the doors!

Membership must be current to enter. We will be selling MDCC memberships at the door.

event.title: British Invasion- MG Exhibit
event.description:
A little British style is rolling into Midwest Dream Car Collection! British Invasion celebrates the charm, character and unmistakable style of classic British automobiles, with a special showcase of MG sports cars.
From sleek roadsters to iconic designs, this exhibit highlights the cars that helped make British motoring a favorite around the world. Come explore the history, craftsmanship and personality behind these distinctive vehicles and experience a little piece of Britain on four wheels!
On display at MDCC Oct. 24th through end of March 2027.

event.title: Open Hood Sunday
event.description: Experience the museum in a whole new way during Open Hood Sunday! Get an up-close look under the hoods of some of our most iconic vehicles as engines are opened and stories come to life. This interactive experience offers a deeper dive into the design, engineering, and history behind the cars—perfect for enthusiasts of all ages. See the details you don’t normally get to see on the showroom floor. Open Hood Sunday takes place the last Sunday of every month, giving you a rare up-close look under the hoods of some of our most iconic vehicles. Join us in March, June, September, and December for Start Up Sunday, when you’ll not only see what’s under the hood—you’ll hear the roar of the engines as they come to life. It’s an unforgettable experience for car lovers of all ages!

event.title: Haunted Horsepower Halloween
event.description:
Halloween is rolling into Midwest Dream Car Collection! Join us Saturday, October 31 for a FREE, family-friendly Halloween celebration!

Bring the kids in their favorite costumes and come trick or treat at the museum! We’ll have plenty of candy, treats and Halloween fun waiting for our little ghosts, goblins, superheroes and car enthusiasts.

🍬 Lots of candy & treats
🎃 Halloween fun for the whole family
🚗 More than 65 incredible cars to explore
👻 Costumes encouraged!
💰 FREE EVENT from 12-4 PM!
